newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends up but trading featureless.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends up but trading featureless.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices were up again at the close but dealers said the rise was prompted by technical adjustments as trading remained featureless.
"There's still no sign of buyers returning to the market," said a trader.

The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board (MRELB) quoted market indicator price for November RSS1 buyer at 313 cents ($1.24) a kg, up 1.50 cents from Tuesday. November SMR 20 was half cent higher at 309.50.
Traders offered the SMR 20 at 306 cents, SMR 10 at 308, SMR 5 at 316, SMR L at 341, SMR CV at 361 and drum latex at 233.
They said the market was void of leads and was only tracking Tokyo futures.
Demand has been poor for Malaysian rubber since major buyers, China, Europe and Middle East, took a back seat after doing active short-covering until August.
The INRO five-day average rose to 240.25 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Oct 29 from 239.47 on Oct 28. The daily indicator was higher at 242.88 against 240.64.
